picks.rationale: Freshest, most actionable craft-tool release: HDR reconstruction from SDR changes finishing, remastering and deliverable pipelines tomorrow.
picks.excerpt: Beeble has released SwitchHDR, a new frontier AI model that reconstructs HDR imagery from conventional SDR video — promising a way to bring dynamic range into footage that never had it, for post, delivery and restoration workflows.

picks.rationale: High-craft, shot-by-shot demo of AI relighting/keying replacing a green-screen pipeline — distinct workflow story that pairs with the SwitchHDR release.
picks.excerpt: Corridor Crew reveals the AI VFX workflow behind their new season: Beeble's SwitchLight AI relighting plus their own CorridorKey keying let them composite actors into scenes without a traditional green-screen pipeline.

picks.rationale: The studios-vs-AI lawsuit turned inside out — Hollywood's own AI use becomes evidence, shaping how openly studios can adopt generative tools.
picks.excerpt: Midjourney is appealing a magistrate judge's order limiting discovery into how Disney, Universal and Warner Bros. themselves use AI in their shows and movies, seeking to put studios' internal AI use on the record as part of its fair-use defense.

picks.rationale: Strongest single angle on the A24×DeepMind story family (explainer kept; Deadline defense and THR boycott pieces dropped as same-story duplicates) — filmmaker-workflow framing of the most consequential studio-AI deal right now.
picks.excerpt: No Film School unpacks A24's $75M research partnership with Google DeepMind — what the studio actually gets (AI storyboard tools, DeepMind researchers working alongside filmmakers) and whether the 'AI is infecting Hollywood' panic fits the facts.

picks.rationale: Voice-cloning consent at its sharpest edge case — minors — setting precedents for likeness and voice rights across screen production.
picks.excerpt: Hasbro's contracts for shows including Peppa Pig allegedly ask child voice actors to sign away rights for AI use of their voices; a UK agents' association warns a parent's approval 'should never be a blanket licence to capture, clone, train, or reuse a child's voice indefinitely.'
